morning: [happy]Morning{you}. I've been up since before the birds. Somebody has to beat them.
Early riser, are you? Good. The best work gets done before the village wakes up.
[happy]Morning. Coffee? No, we haven't got coffee. Hot water and willpower, then.
afternoon: Afternoon{you}. Half the day's gone and I've only fixed three things. Shameful.
[happy]Ah, good. You can hold the other end of this plank while we talk.
Afternoon. If you've come to tell me to rest, don't. If you've come to help, grab a nail.
evening: [happy]Evening{you}. Hammer's down, boots are off in spirit if not in fact.
Evening. This is the only hour of the day my shoulders stop arguing with me.
[happy]You caught me resting. Don't tell anyone. I have a reputation.
night: [surprised]What are you doing up? Can't sleep either? The wind's rattling the north shutters again.
It's late{you}. If something's broken, it can wait till morning. Probably.
Night owl, eh? I check the fences at night sometimes. Old habit.

rain: [worried]Rain. Every drop is a leak I haven't found yet.
Rain's good for one thing: it shows you where the roof is lying to you.
[laughing]I'm soaked to the bone and the timber's swelling. Lovely day, isn't it?
clear: [happy]Dry weather. Perfect for tarring roofs. Want to help? It's very fun. That's a lie.
Clear skies. Wood cuts clean, glue sets fast. Days like this I could build a cathedral.
[happy]Good light today. You can see every crooked line. Which is good and bad.
storm: [worried]Storm's coming. I'm going round every house to check the shutters. You should stay inside.
Hear that wind? Old buildings talk in storms. I listen for the ones that sound scared.

work: Can't stop long. This beam won't raise itself, and I won't let Tomas see it crooked.
[happy]Mind the saw. I'm in the middle of something and it's actually going well, for once.
gather: Hauling timber. Ask me how my back is. Actually, don't.
Collecting offcuts. You'd be amazed what you can build from what other people throw away.
rest: I'm resting. Officially. Unofficially I'm planning the next roof.
[happy]Feet up. Don't let me catch you telling anyone I sat down.
socialize: [laughing]I'm being sociable. Elias insists. Apparently grunting at people doesn't count.
Lunch at the fire. Best part of the day, though I'd never admit it to the others.
trade: Buying nails. Sera's prices are criminal, but she does carry good iron.
Haggling. Badly. I'm better at building than bargaining.
explore: Just walking. I like to see the village from outside it now and then. Spot the sagging roofs.
Looking for good oak. The woods past the river have some fine old trees.
sleep: Mm? It's the middle of the night. Unless something's on fire, come back tomorrow.

tired: [sad]I'm worn thin today. Too many jobs and not enough hands.
Don't mind me. I'm running on stubbornness and stale bread.
[worried]If I sit down I won't get up again, so I'm standing. Talk fast.
worried: [worried]Something's not right. I can feel it like a crack in a wall you can't see yet.
[worried]Sorry. Head's elsewhere. Thinking about whether we're ready for winter.
I keep counting what could go wrong. It's a builder thing. And a Mara thing.
happy: [happy]Good day today. Everything I touched stayed where I put it.
[laughing]I'm in a good mood, so ask me for favours now. It won't last.
[happy]Finished the fence by the pasture. Straight as an arrow. I may frame it.
busy: Busy. Very busy. Talk while I work, if you can keep up.
I've got three jobs and two hands. Make it quick, unless you're offering a third hand.

stranger: You're new. I like to know who's in my village. What can you do with your hands?
We'll get on fine if you don't lean on anything I've just built.
friend: [happy]You're alright, you know. You show up when it counts.
I trust you with my good saw. That's not a small thing.
close: [happy]You're one of the few people I'd let help me with a roof. That's practically a marriage proposal around here.
I don't say this much, so listen: I'm glad you're here.
[laughing]You've seen me covered in tar and swearing at a ladder. We're past formalities.
wary: I'm watching you. Prove me wrong.
You've got a lot of making up to do.

childhood: I grew up in a mill town downriver. My father fixed the waterwheels. I learned to climb before I learned to read.
When I was small I built a treehouse so ugly the birds refused to nest in it. I was so proud of it.
[laughing]I broke my arm falling off a roof when I was nine. Climbed straight back up the week the splint came off.
My mother wanted me to be a seamstress. I sewed my sleeve to my skirt on the first day. That settled that.
family: My father taught me that a house is a promise you make to people you'll never meet. He's gone now. I keep his square.
I've two brothers somewhere east. We write when we remember. We mostly don't remember.
[sad]My mother still thinks I'll come home and marry a miller. I send her drawings of the houses instead.
Tomas is the nearest thing to family I've got here. He'd hate that I said it.
background: I came here with Tomas when this place was a clearing and a stubborn idea. We put up the first walls together.
I left the mill town because nobody would hire a woman to build anything bigger than a henhouse. Here, I build what's needed.
First winter here, the snow came early and we slept five to a hut. I swore every house after would be warm.
work: People think building is about strength. It's about patience. And spite, a little. Spite is very good for finishing things.
A good joint doesn't need nails. A bad one needs a miracle.
Every house in this village leans a hair to the east. That's the wind. I build them leaning west so they end up straight.
I check every beam twice and every promise three times. Beams don't lie, people sometimes do.
[happy]The best part of a build is the first night someone sleeps under it and doesn't know they're safe because of you.
skills: I can frame a cottage in four days with two helpers who listen, or nine days with two who don't.
I can tell what wood is by the sound it makes when you knock it. Oak sounds smug. Pine sounds cheerful.
[laughing]I can also throw a hammer and hit a post at twenty paces. Not useful. Very satisfying.
hobbies: I carve little houses out of offcuts. The children use them for games. Don't tell them I made them.
[happy]I walk the bridge at sunset and count the boards. Forty-one. It's always forty-one. I still count.
I collect old hinges. Every one has a story. Mostly the story is 'rusted'.
ambitions: [happy]I want to build a proper hall. Big enough for the whole village to eat under one roof in winter.
One day I'll build a stone bridge. One that'll still be standing when nobody remembers my name. That's the dream.
I want this to be a town people walk towards, not past.
home: My house is the plainest one in the village. A builder's house always is. No time to fuss over your own.
I've got a workbench where most people keep a table. I eat standing up. Elias despairs of me.
My roof has never leaked. Not once. I check it after every storm anyway, out of pride.
furniture: A chair should hold you up without you noticing it. If you notice a chair, it's failed.
I made my bed from the first oak we felled here. It creaks like an old dog. I wouldn't change it.
[laughing]Tomas makes the pretty furniture. I make the furniture that survives a winter. We argue about which matters more.
village: Every board here has a story. That fence? Elias and I put it up in a hailstorm because the cows wouldn't wait.
[happy]When I came, there was mud and a fire. Now there are streets, if you squint. I squint a lot.
This place is held together by stubborn people and good joinery. Mostly the people.
friendship: I don't make friends quickly. I make them like I make walls: slowly, and they stay up.
A friend is someone who holds the ladder without being asked.
[happy]I'm loyal to a fault. Ask anyone. Actually, don't ask Sera, she'll make up a story.
disagreements: Tomas and I argued for a week about whether to use pegs or nails on the storehouse. We used both. Neither of us is happy.
[angry]Sera once sold my good chisel to a passing tinker. 'It looked unloved,' she said. It was in my toolbox!
I tell people when they're wrong. Some of them thank me for it. Eventually.
animals: Animals are fine. Animals don't argue about where the door should go.
There's a fox that watches me work from the woodline. I call him Foreman. He never helps either.
[laughing]Elias's goat ate my measuring string once. I measured that roof by eye. It's still standing. The goat looked smug for a month.
nature: The river decides where we build, not me. You learn to listen to water or it teaches you the hard way.
I love a good tree. Mostly so I can cut it down and turn it into something useful. Then I plant two more. Fair's fair.
Nia says every plant has a purpose. Most of the ones I meet seem to exist to grow in my foundations.
seasons: Spring is for fixing what winter broke. Summer is for building new. Autumn's for panic. Winter's for regret.
[happy]Autumn's my favourite. Cold enough to work hard, warm enough not to freeze doing it.
Winter is when you find out who built their house properly. I like being right in winter.
mornings: Mornings are honest. The light shows you exactly what you did wrong yesterday.
I like to walk the village at dawn and listen for doors that stick. A sticking door is a cry for help.
evenings: Evenings by the fire are where the best plans get made and the worst songs get sung.
[happy]I sit by my window in the evening and watch the smoke from every chimney. Each one's a house still standing.
events: Festivals are nice. People dance on floors I laid. That's my kind of applause.
[worried]When the raids come, I'm on the walls with a hammer. It's the only tool I need for monsters and nails alike.
Every time someone new moves in I measure them for a house in my head. Can't help it.
worries: [worried]I worry I'm the only one who knows how half these buildings are put together. If I fell off a roof tomorrow, who'd fix them?
[worried]The storehouse roof has one winter left in it. Maybe two if the gods like us.
I worry about the children playing on the timber stack. I've told them a hundred times. They're children. They hear 'climb'.
hopes: [happy]I hope someone young wants to learn the trade. I'd teach them everything. Even the swearing.
I hope one day nobody in this village has to sleep cold. Then I'll retire. Maybe.
I'd like to see a second street. Then a market square. Then a town hall. Then I'll sit down.
surprises: [surprised]Elias brought me lunch yesterday without me asking. Nobody's done that since my mother.
[surprised]I found a swallow's nest in the rafters of the storehouse. I built around it. Don't tell anyone I'm soft.
funny: [laughing]Tomas once lectured me for an hour on the right way to hold a chisel. He was holding it upside down the whole time.
[laughing]I nailed my own coat to a wall once. Stood there for ten minutes pretending I meant to be leaning on it.
[laughing]Sera tried to help me build a fence. She painted it instead. Bright red. The cows won't go near it.

elias: [happy]Elias is the best of us. He'd give you his last loaf and ask if you wanted butter.
Elias is too soft for his own good. That's why we all keep an eye on him.
If Elias ever gets angry, run. I've seen it once. A crow learned a lesson that day.
nia: Nia's clever. Too clever. She asked me why wood floats and I had to admit I didn't know.
[laughing]Nia patched my hand once with something green and smelly. Healed in a day. Smelled for a week.
She asks a hundred questions a day. Forty of them are good. That's a better rate than most.
tomas: Tomas taught me everything. He'll tell you so, often.
[happy]Tomas grumbles like a rusty gate, but he made every child in this village a toy. By hand.
Don't let Tomas fool you. He's the softest old man you'll ever meet. Just don't touch his tools.
sera: [laughing]Sera could sell sand to a desert. She sold me a hammer I already owned.
Sera's trouble. The good kind, mostly. Like a loose plank you get fond of.
I don't believe half of Sera's stories. The other half, I've seen her do. That's what worries me.

achievement: [happy]Heard you {thing}. Not bad. Not bad at all.
So you {thing}. You keep surprising me. I don't like surprises, but I like that one.
gift: [surprised]For me? You didn't have to. I'll use it. That's the best thanks I know.
[happy]A gift? Nobody gives builders gifts. They give us lists of things to fix.
house: [happy]I saw your house. The corners are true. I checked. Twice.
Your house is standing. That's the main thing. The second thing is it's actually nice. Don't let it go to your head.
discovery: You found {thing}? I've been meaning to go out there and check it's still standing.
[happy]Exploring, eh? Bring me back a nice piece of oak next time.

new_home: [happy]My new house still smells of fresh sawdust. Best smell in the world.
I've built a hundred homes and never lived in a new one till now. It's strange. Good strange.
partner: [happy]I never thought I'd share a roof with anyone. Turns out I like the company. Don't spread that around.
Having someone to come home to changes how you build. You build for two.
child: [happy]My little one already has a hammer. A wooden one. Tomas made it. They hit everything with it.
I'm teaching my child to measure twice. They mostly measure the cat.
friend: [happy]I've got more friends here than I ever had back home. Funny what a few years of roofs will do.
I keep a list of people I'd trust with my life. It's getting longer. That's new.
grief: [sad]I made the coffin myself. It's the hardest thing I've ever built. It was the best one, too.
[sad]Some days I walk past their door and nearly knock.

stories: Want to hear about the first winter? Fine. Sit.
Five of us, one hut, and snow up to the window. Tomas told the same story every night for a month.
By the end we could recite it with him. We still do, at festivals. He pretends to be annoyed.
[happy]That's when I knew we'd make it. People who can laugh at the same bad story can survive anything.
I'll tell you about the bridge.
The first one washed away in the spring flood. I'd built it too low. My fault.
I sat on the bank and cried for an hour. Then Elias sat next to me and didn't say anything for another hour.
[happy]Then we built the second one. Higher. It's still there. Every time I cross it, I remember both of those hours.
Here's one I don't tell often.
Back in the mill town, I built a whole barn on my own, in secret, at night, to prove I could.
The owner came out in the morning, saw it, and asked which man had built it.
[angry]I said, 'The one standing in front of you.' He laughed. I left the next week. Best decision I ever made.
When she first arrived she tried to sell me a 'magic level' that was always straight.
It was a plank with a line painted on it. I bought it. I still use it to prop the door open.
[happy]She's never let me forget it. I've never let her forget I paid in buttons.

questions.ask: Here's a question. If you could build anything at all, what would it be?

react.house: [happy]A house. Good answer. The best things are the simple ones.
react.tower: [laughing]A tower? Ambitious. I like ambitious. I'd want to check the foundations first.
react.bridge: [happy]A bridge! Now we're talking. Bridges bring people together. Literally.
react.boat: A boat? Hm. Same skills, wetter consequences.
react.other: {answer}? Never built one of those. Yet.

questions.recall: You told me you'd build {answer}, given the chance. I've been thinking about how I'd do it.

questions.ask: Are you good with your hands? Honestly.

react.yes: [happy]Good. I'll put you to work then. Don't make me regret it.
react.no: [laughing]Honest, at least. Hands can learn. Pride can't.
react.learning: [happy]That's the right answer. Everyone's learning. Even me. Don't tell Tomas.
react.other: That's not a yes or a no, but I'll take it.

recall.yes: You said you're good with your hands. I've got a job that needs them, when you're ready.
recall.no: You said you're not much use with your hands. Nobody is, at first. Offer's open.
recall.learning: You said you're still learning with your hands. How's it going? Show me sometime.
recall.other: I haven't forgotten what you said about working with your hands.

questions.ask: Which season do you like best? I'm curious. Don't say winter, it's a trick.

react.spring: Spring. Fixing season. You'll fit right in.
react.summer: [happy]Summer. Long days, dry wood. Good choice.
react.autumn: [happy]Autumn! Same as me. I knew there was a reason I liked you.
react.winter: [laughing]Winter. I said don't say winter. You're as stubborn as me.
react.other: {answer}? That's not a season I've heard of, but alright.

questions.recall: You like {answer} best, you said. Not my pick, but I respect it.

questions.ask: Are you planning to stay? In the village, I mean. For good.

react.yes: [happy]Good. Then I'll build things that last for you.
react.no: [sad]Hm. Well. Make the most of it while you're here.
react.maybe: Maybe's honest. Stay long enough and the place grows on you. Like moss.
react.other: That's not an answer. But I suppose that's an answer.

recall.yes: You said you'd stay. I'm holding you to it.
recall.no: You said you might not stay. I hope we've changed your mind.
recall.maybe: You said maybe, about staying. Still maybe? I'll take maybe.
recall.other: I remember what you said about staying.
